cargo build --release
cargo install alacritty

cargo build --release --no-default-features --features=wayland
This means you won't find things like tabs or splits (which are best left to a window manager or terminal multiplexer)

By default you can start a selection using v and copy it using y. All selection modes that are available with the mouse can be accessed from vi mode, including the semantic (Alt v), line (Shift v) and block selection (Ctrl v).
Search allows you to find anything in Alacritty's scrollback buffer. You can search forward using Ctrl Shift f (Command f on macOS) and backward using Ctrl Shift b (Command b on macOS).
The `SearchStart` and `SearchEnd` keybinding actions can be bound if you're looking for a way to jump to the start or the end of a match.

After making a selection, you can use the right mouse button to expand it. Double-clicking will expand the selection semantically, while triple-clicking will perform line selection. If you hold Ctrl while expanding the selection, it will switch to the block selection mode.
You can open URLs with your mouse by clicking on them. The modifiers required to be held and program which should open the URL can be setup in the configuration file.
Colors are specified using their hexadecimal values with a _#_ prefix: _#RRGGBB_.

Blank space added around the window in pixels. This padding is scaled by DPI and the specified value is always added at both opposing sides.
Offset is the extra space around each character. _y_ can be thought of as modifying the line spacing, and _x_ as modifying the letter spacing.

Alacritty is a modern terminal emulator that comes with sensible defaults, but allows for extensive configuration.
live_config_reload = true | false ... Default: true
All key-value pairs in the [env] section will be added as environment variables for any process spawned by Alacritty, including its shell.
Directory the shell is started in. When this is unset, or "None", the working directory of the parent process will be used.
Background opacity as a floating point number from 0.0 to 1.0. The value 0.0 is completely transparent and 1.0 is opaque.
decorations = "Full" | "None" | "Transparent" | "Buttonless"
normal = { family = "<string>", style = "<string>" } ... size = <float> Font size in points.
Offset is the extra space around each character. y can be thought of as modifying the line spacing, and x as modifying the letter spacing.
Alacritty will use a custom built-in font for box drawing characters (Unicode points U+2500 - U+259F), legacy computing symbols
startup_mode = "Windowed" | "Maximized" | "Fullscreen" | "SimpleFullscreen"
AlwaysOnTop — Window is a toplevel window.
Maximum number of lines in the scrollback buffer. Specifying 0 will disable scrolling. Limited to 100000.
Make Option key behave as Alt.
Number of lines/columns (not pixels) in the terminal.
Allow terminal applications to change Alacritty's window title.
Early user: "It really is the fastest one I ever used. Font rendering is great."
Installation was surprisingly easy and performance surprisingly good: a `find /Applications` crashed Hyper, took 1:28 in iTerm2, 0:32 in Terminal and 0:20 in Alacritty.

User who keeps tmux panes watching fast-scrolling logs while working in another pane says rendering speed was what held tmux back. The lack of scrollback and tabs doesn't bother them because they use tmux for that.

Complaint about the minimalism: the user needs scrollback (to grab text with the mouse), tabs, and activity/silence monitoring. They won't start tmux at every local prompt just to use Alacritty, so they can't use it until the author reconsiders.
Early pre-alpha build crashed for one user with panics in the pty reader thread: 'index out of bounds: the len is 24 but the index is 24' and 'cursor fell off grid'.
User put off by the build instructions requiring a pinned Rust nightly compiler: "Ok, I'll... um not do that. Hope you publish a build soon though!"

Commenter says Ctrl-C can take forever on an accidental cat of a 1GB file in many emulators. They credit Alacritty's approach of locking refresh to the screen rate and rendering only current data with making it much more responsive.
On the long-standing ligature issue: "Kind of given up hope that there will ever be any support for it." Another user switched to Kitty long ago because missing ligatures were a deal breaker.
"Ligatures is definitely a nice-to-have, not a must. I really enjoy Alacritty and use it every day. The performance is amazing!"
User appreciates how simple and not bloated Alacritty is, compared to software bloated with features that are only useful in edge cases.
Former kitty user found its CPU usage high, tried Alacritty, but the lack of tabs was a deal-breaker. They switched to WezTerm instead.
User last rebuilt Alacritty a year or more ago and hasn't felt a burning desire for new features.
"Used it, its everything you need most likely."

Complaint: Alacritty doesn't handle modifier keys well, and many neovim shortcuts with control/alt don't work unless you add escape-sequence keybindings to the config. Some distros ship such a config, but it breaks things like Ctrl+A to jump to line start. They recommend foot.

Counterpoint: on Ubuntu with tmux and fish, Ctrl+A works and all tmux/fish shortcuts, including custom tab-like Ctrl bindings, worked without any Alacritty configuration. Another user of Alacritty with neovim also reports no such issues.
Never had issues with Alacritty and neovim, but finds foot much faster.

Tried it on Windows with WSL2: hit config gotchas from the switch to TOML, and couldn't get M+PgUp/PgDn and S-Left/Right shortcuts working with tmux and neovim. Saw no benefits and went back to Windows Terminal.

Nordic keyboard layout user (å, ä, ö) found the extra characters a pain when binding key combinations. Another macOS user says the app doesn't use the OS to resolve keystrokes, so their keyboard layout doesn't work at all.
Long-time Alacritty user moved to WezTerm because built-in tabs and windows mean they no longer need tmux. WezTerm also supports ligatures and Lua config.
User says kitty would hang for a minute or two on garbled Unicode (e.g. accidentally catting a binary file). They switched to Alacritty because it doesn't have this problem.
